{{distinguish|Grothendieck–Ogg–Shafarevich formula}}

In [[mathematics]], the '''Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich criterion''' states that if <math>A</math> is an [[elliptic curve]] or [[abelian variety]] over a [[local field]] <math>K</math>, and <math>\ell</math> is a [[prime number|prime]] not dividing the characteristic of the [[residue field]] of <math>K</math>, then <math>A</math> has good reduction if and only if the <math>\ell</math>-adic [[Tate module]] <math>T_\ell</math> of <math>A</math> is [[Ramification of Galois representations|unramified]]. 

[[Andrew Ogg]] introduced the criterion for elliptic curves.{{sfnp|Ogg|1967}} [[Jean-Pierre Serre]] and [[John Tate (mathematician)|John Tate]]{{sfnp|Serre|Tate|1968}} used the results of [[André Néron]]{{sfnp|Néron|1964}} to extend it to abelian varieties,
and named the criterion after Ogg, Néron and [[Igor Shafarevich]] (commenting that Ogg's result seems to have been known to Shafarevich).
